intro.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that merges two sorted lists into a single sorted list. You will learn the core concept of the two-pointer technique, which efficiently compares elements from each list. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, while loops, and conditional logic. This exercise will help you understand how to combine data in order, a common task in algorithms and data processing. By the end, you'll have a working solution that handles lists of varying lengths.
intro.usecase: Merging sorted lists is a fundamental pattern in data processing and user interfaces. For example, a social media feed might need to combine two chronologically sorted streams of posts—one from friends and one from trending topics—into a single, unified timeline. Similarly, an e-commerce dashboard could merge sorted lists of products from different inventory sources to display a consolidated, ranked catalog. As a developer, you'll use this algorithm to efficiently handle sorted data from APIs, databases, or user inputs in features like merged search results, activity logs, or real-time notification feeds.
